brief: Academy Securities' Peter Tchir reviews the post-FOMC tape: the 10-year sold off through the week to just under 5% and the yen broke support at 155, closing 156.9. The Houthis are hitting Saudi energy infrastructure, including jet fuel facilities, rather than US assets. Pipeline damage from an earlier strike looks more extensive than first thought, so Tchir argues disruptions to energy complexes outside the US/Iran conflict should be priced in. Diesel has broken through last week's flagged chart level, a mounting inflation pressure he says export restrictions won't meaningfully fix, since domestic price still tracks global price minus transport and storage. On Iran, the sanctions blockade is working but won't force a deal in weeks. One floated alternative is securing the Strait-controlling islands, possibly through Kharg, after the midterms, when political risk to Trump is lower. A Greenland deal was announced with terms undisclosed. The Trump/Xi summit's focus has shifted to cyber, AI and compute, with cheap Chinese compute a concern and a downside bias on the compute-spend story. Bottom line: energy prices and rates likely move higher.
